content.text: FacebookLog InLog InForgot Account?REVOLT's PostREVOLT Verified accountApril 1 at 9:00 PM · Shared with PublicNASA is set to launch Artemis II today in a history-making mission that will send astronauts around the Moon for the first time since Apollo 17 in 1972. The four-person crew, made up of Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen, is expected to lift off aboard NASA’s Space Launch System rocket from Kennedy Space Center.Unlike the Apollo missions that landed astronauts on the lunar surface, Artemis II is a 10-day crewed flyby mission designed to test NASA’s Orion spacecraft, life-support systems, communications, and deep-space operations before future Moon landing missions. The mission is a major step in NASA’s broader Artemis program, which aims to return humans to the Moon and build toward long-term exploration beyond Earth.The launch also carries historic milestones. Christina Koch is set to become the first woman to travel beyond low-Earth orbit toward the Moon, Victor Glover the first Black astronaut on a lunar mission, and Jeremy Hansen the first Canadian to take part in a mission around the Moon.
